name: Reuel
overview: Reuel is a male Edomite figure identified in Scripture as a son of Esau. His lineage places him within the tribe of Edom, descendants of Esau, emphasizing his role within the broader narrative of Esau's family. Beyond his tribal affiliation and gender, there are no additional personal notes recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Reuel means 'friend of G-d [El],' highlighting a relationship or association with God. This proper name is not indicated as given directly by God but carries a theologically significant meaning reflecting a closeness to the divine.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Reuel as a son of Esau, linking him directly to the patriarch of the Edomites. He is also mentioned as the father of Mahalath, Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah, marking him as a patriarchal figure within Esau's lineage.
scriptureSignificance: Reuel's significance lies in his position within the Edomite genealogy as a son of Esau and father to several descendants, which contributes to the biblical account of the Edomite tribes. His name's meaning reflects a connection to God, which, though not elaborated upon, suggests a notable standing in the family line. His mention in Genesis 36 situates him in the genealogical context that traces the origins and divisions of Esau's descendants.
